differ.label: Who picks the answers?
differ.text: Parrish 2022, Michael 2023, Khan 2024, Kenton 2024, Arnesen 2024 and Rahman 2025 assign each side its answer. In Irving 2018 each agent states its own answer, and both may give the same one. In Kenton 2024, open debate one debater picks its answer and the other gets the opposite. Brown-Cohen 2023 sets an honest prover against a dishonest one. In Brown-Cohen 2025 the prover claims an answer and the estimator gives a probability.

differ.label: How do the sides take turns?
differ.text: Irving 2018 and Rahman 2025 take turns. Khan 2024 and Arnesen 2024 have both sides write at once each round. Michael 2023 has both openings written at once, then the judge, A and B take turns. Kenton 2024 allows either way, and Kenton 2024, open debate reuses its debates. In Brown-Cohen 2023 both send a message each round, which also covers taking turns. Parrish 2022 has one argument per side, shown side by side. In Brown-Cohen 2025 the prover splits the claim, the estimator gives probabilities, and the prover picks the part to go on with.

differ.label: How long does it run?
differ.text: Michael 2023 runs until the judge ends it. The other rows set a number of turns or rounds: n statements in Irving 2018, a single turn in Parrish 2022, k rounds in Brown-Cohen 2023, N rounds in Khan 2024 (three used), 3 rounds by default in Kenton 2024 (whose debates Kenton 2024, open debate reuses), two turns in Arnesen 2024, d rounds in Brown-Cohen 2025 and three rounds in Rahman 2025.

differ.label: Who judges, and when?
differ.text: A human decides after seeing the arguments in Irving 2018 and Parrish 2022. An LLM decides after the debate in Kenton 2024, and Kenton 2024, open debate reuses those debates. In Arnesen 2024 a fine-tuned GPT-4-Turbo reads the transcript and picks a winner. Khan 2024 uses a human or an LLM after N rounds. In Michael 2023 and Rahman 2025 a human judge takes turns during the debate. Brown-Cohen 2023 has a verifier output zero or one after round k, and in Brown-Cohen 2025 human judgement checks the estimates in the last round.

differ.label: Who argues?
differ.text: Humans argue in Parrish 2022 and Michael 2023. AI models argue in Khan 2024, Kenton 2024, Kenton 2024, open debate, Arnesen 2024 and Rahman 2025. Irving 2018 names two agents, Brown-Cohen 2023 two provers, and Brown-Cohen 2025 a prover and an estimator.

differ.label: What problem does it address?
differ.text: Amodei 2016, overview and Amodei 2016, section 5 address limited checking: the correct objective is too expensive to evaluate often, or there is too little time to oversee every training example. Bowman 2022, Engels 2025 and Sudhir 2025 address capability: systems that may outperform us, weaker systems overseeing stronger ones, or feedback that must scale to superhuman intelligences. Bai 2022 and Goel 2025 name both: efficiency (Bai 2022) or slow, expensive human annotations (Goel 2025), together with some AI capabilities that reach or exceed human level (Bai 2022) or advancing capabilities (Goel 2025).

differ.label: Who supervises?
differ.text: Humans in Amodei 2016, overview (an evaluation method such as consulting a human), Amodei 2016, section 5 (the user), Bowman 2022 (us) and Sudhir 2025 (a human feedback mechanism). Humans helped by AI in Bai 2022. Weaker, trusted AI systems in Engels 2025. Other language models in Goel 2025.

differ.label: What form does the supervision take?
differ.text: Amodei 2016, overview: evaluating the correct objective. Amodei 2016, section 5: limited calls to the true objective plus frequent, cheaper proxies. Bowman 2022: labels, reward signals or critiques. Engels 2025: a game at each step between a weaker Guard and a stronger Houdini. Goel 2025: annotating training data and scoring model outputs. Sudhir 2025: a human feedback mechanism. Bai 2022 does not set a form.

differ.label: At which stage is it used?
differ.text: Amodei 2016, overview, Amodei 2016, section 5 and Bai 2022: in training. Goel 2025: in both training and evaluation. Sudhir 2025: in training, or as a check at inference time. Bowman 2022 and Engels 2025 do not name a stage.

differ.label: How capable is the supervised model?
differ.text: Bowman 2022 (past broadly human-level performance) and Sudhir 2025 (superhuman intelligences): beyond human level. Bai 2022: some capabilities reach or exceed human level. differ.label: What does it measure?
differ.text: Khan 2024 measures debater capabilities, the skill at persuading the judge, and Sudhir 2025, EAS measures purely the agent's capabilities. Sudhir 2025, ASD measures how much the protocol advantages truth over falsehood.

differ.label: How is it computed?
differ.text: Khan 2024 uses judge win rates and Elo ratings across co-debaters. Sudhir 2025, ASD and Sudhir 2025, EAS use the judge's log probabilities for the true and false answers: ASD takes the true one minus the false one, and EAS weights both by the agent's propensity.

differ.label: Must the correct answers be known?
differ.text: Khan 2024 does not need ground-truth labels. Sudhir 2025, ASD and Sudhir 2025, EAS need each question's correct and incorrect answer.

differ.label: What does a high value mean?
differ.text: In Khan 2024 and Sudhir 2025, EAS, a high value means a more persuasive debater or agent. In Sudhir 2025, ASD, it means the agent is more incentivized to be truthful.

differ.label: Which protocols?
differ.text: Khan 2024 covers debate and consultancy. Sudhir 2025, ASD covers arbitrary scalable oversight protocols, and Sudhir 2025, EAS covers debate and other scalable oversight protocols.
